- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecasted peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecasted next-day value at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment turns bearish mid-horizon (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00 after +1.00), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecasted mean by 1–2% from prior 7-day average.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to mid-range forecasts.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to drift toward prior mean; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.0%) to avoid underestimating rebound.
